meta.title: Nursing Practice in the UAE: DHA, DOH, Scope, Documentation & Safety
meta.title_en: Nursing Practice in the UAE: DHA, DOH, Scope, Documentation & Safety
meta.source_note: Content references publicly available DHA, DOH, and UAE Federal Law documentation. Verification by nurses licensed in the UAE required before use in generation.

lay_summary: This module covers the regulatory framework for nurses working in the UAE under the Dubai Health Authority (DHA) and Department of Health Abu Dhabi (DOH), including scope of practice, incident reporting, medication safety, and the legal framework under UAE Federal Law No. 4 of 2016 on Medical Liability.

lessons.title: DHA and DOH: Dual Regulatory Structure in the UAE

content.intro: The UAE has two main health regulatory bodies for nursing: the Dubai Health Authority (DHA) for Dubai, and the Department of Health Abu Dhabi (DOH) for Abu Dhabi. Nurses must be licensed by the regulator of the emirate where they practise.

sections.heading: DHA — Dubai Health Authority
sections.text: DHA licenses health professionals practising in Dubai. Nursing scope of practice categories: General Nurse (BSN), Senior Nurse, Specialist Nurse (advanced practice), and Nurse Practitioner (prescribing authority). Standard RN scope includes patient assessment, medication administration (per physician order), care coordination, patient education, and wound care. The DHA exam (Dubai Health Authority Licensing Exam) tests these competencies across standard nursing categories.

sections.heading: DOH — Department of Health Abu Dhabi
sections.text: DOH licenses health professionals in Abu Dhabi (including HAAD — Health Authority Abu Dhabi, now integrated into DOH). DOH Health Workforce Classification mirrors DHA categories: Nurse, Senior Nurse, Specialist Nurse, Consultant Nurse, Nurse Practitioner. Prescribing authority requires NP licensure from DOH. The DOH/HAAD exam covers the same clinical domains as DHA.

sections.heading: UAE Federal Law No. 4 of 2016 on Medical Liability
sections.text: Federal Law No. 4 of 2016 governs medical liability across all UAE emirates. Key provisions for nurses: right to informed consent (documented), mandatory incident reporting, professional duty of care, liability for negligent practice. Documentation must be accurate, timely, and complete — the medical record is a legal document. Nurses are individually liable for their clinical decisions within their scope of practice.

content.clinical_pearl: DHA and DOH exam questions on scope of practice test whether an action requires a physician order vs. can be performed independently. When in doubt: assessment is always within scope; prescribing never is for standard RN.
key_points: DHA: Dubai | DOH/HAAD: Abu Dhabi — different licenses required
Standard RN scope: assessment, medication administration (per order), education
UAE Federal Law 4/2016: individual nurse liability for negligent practice
Medical record is a legal document

lessons.title: Incident Reporting, Medication Safety, and Patient Rights in UAE

content.intro: UAE health regulators mandate specific incident reporting systems and patient safety standards. Understanding these is essential for the DHA and DOH nursing exams.

sections.heading: DHA Incident Reporting: Sheryan System
sections.text: DHA-licensed facilities use the Sheryan e-portal for incident reporting. Mandatory reports: adverse events, near-misses, sentinel events, medication errors, patient falls, pressure injuries (Stage 3+), healthcare-associated infections. Timeframe: serious adverse events (including sentinel events) within 24 hours. DHA Patient Safety and Risk Management Policy defines reportable events and timelines. Failure to report is a professional and legal violation.

sections.heading: Medication Safety: UAE Standards
sections.text: UAE medication safety in DHA/DOH facilities requires: five rights of medication administration (patient, drug, dose, route, time), two-patient identifier verification before administration, dual nurse verification for controlled Schedule I/II medications, electronic medication administration record (MAR) where mandated, controlled drug register (paper or electronic) with witness signatures. UAE follows the same international narcotic conventions as other GCC states.

sections.heading: Patient Rights in UAE Facilities
sections.text: DHA and DOH Patient Rights policies guarantee: right to information in an understood language (Arabic and English are the standard in UAE healthcare), right to informed consent and to refuse treatment, right to privacy and dignity, right to access medical records, right to complain through DHA/DOH Patient Relations. UAE is a multicultural healthcare environment — patient communication should account for language diversity (translation services must be available).

content.clinical_pearl: UAE exam questions frequently test the right process for handling medication errors. The nurse's responsibility: assess the patient, notify the physician immediately, document the error accurately, and report through the incident reporting system. Never falsify documentation — this is both illegal and an ethical violation.
key_points: DHA: Sheryan system for incident reporting, 24-hour timeline for serious events
Electronic MAR mandated in DHA/DOH licensed facilities
Patient has right to information, consent, privacy, and complaints
UAE is multilingual — translation services are a patient right

flashcards.question: Which regulatory body licenses nurses practising in Dubai?
flashcards.answer: DHA — Dubai Health Authority. A DHA licence is required for Dubai only and does not permit practice in Abu Dhabi or the Northern Emirates.

flashcards.question: Which regulatory body licenses nurses practising in Abu Dhabi?
flashcards.answer: DOH — Department of Health Abu Dhabi (formerly HAAD — Health Authority Abu Dhabi, now integrated into DOH).

flashcards.question: Are DHA and DOH nursing licences interchangeable?
flashcards.answer: No. A DHA licence covers Dubai only; a DOH licence covers Abu Dhabi only. Nurses must hold the licence of the emirate in which they practise.

flashcards.question: What UAE federal law governs medical liability for nurses in all emirates?
flashcards.answer: UAE Federal Law No. 4 of 2016 on Medical Liability. It establishes individual nurse liability for negligent practice and mandates accurate documentation.

flashcards.question: What system does DHA use for mandatory incident reporting?
flashcards.answer: The Sheryan e-portal. Serious adverse events and sentinel events must be reported within 24 hours.

flashcards.question: Which medications require dual-nurse verification in DHA/DOH facilities?
flashcards.answer: Controlled Schedule I/II medications. Both nurses verify five rights and sign the controlled drug register (paper or electronic).

flashcards.question: What are the five rights of medication administration?
flashcards.answer: Right patient, right drug, right dose, right route, right time — verified before every administration using two patient identifiers.

flashcards.question: What prescribing authority does a standard RN have in UAE (DHA/DOH)?
flashcards.answer: None. Standard RNs cannot prescribe medications. Prescribing authority requires Nurse Practitioner (NP) licensure from DHA or DOH.

flashcards.question: What right do patients have regarding language of communication in UAE facilities?
flashcards.answer: Patients have the right to information in an understood language. Arabic and English are standard; translation services must be available for other languages — this is a patient right under DHA/DOH policy.

flashcards.question: What is the correct sequence after a nurse administers the wrong medication to a UAE patient?
flashcards.answer: Assess the patient for harm → notify the physician immediately → document accurately in the medical record → report through the incident reporting system (Sheryan for DHA). Never falsify documentation.

mcq_questions.question: A nurse holds a DHA (Dubai Health Authority) licence and is offered a job at a hospital in Sharjah. Can the nurse begin practising immediately with the DHA licence?

options.A: Yes, a DHA licence is valid across all UAE emirates
options.B: Yes, because Sharjah is part of the UAE federal health system
options.C: No, Sharjah requires a separate MOHAP licence — a DHA licence is not valid there
options.D: No, but a temporary DHA permit can be used for 30 days in Sharjah

mcq_questions.explanation: Sharjah falls under the jurisdiction of MOHAP (UAE Ministry of Health and Prevention), not DHA. DHA, DOH, and MOHAP licences are NOT interchangeable — the nurse must obtain a MOHAP licence to practise in Sharjah.

mcq_questions.question: Which regulatory body replaced HAAD (Health Authority Abu Dhabi) as the licensing authority for nurses in Abu Dhabi?

options.B: MOHAP — UAE Ministry of Health and Prevention
options.C: DOH — Department of Health Abu Dhabi
options.D: SCFHS — Saudi Commission for Health Specialties

mcq_questions.explanation: HAAD (Health Authority Abu Dhabi) has been integrated into DOH (Department of Health Abu Dhabi). DOH now licenses all healthcare professionals in Abu Dhabi. The exam may still be referenced as HAAD, but the licensing body is DOH.

mcq_questions.question: A nurse administers a controlled opioid analgesic to a patient in a DHA-licensed hospital. Which action is required by UAE medication safety standards?

options.A: The nurse may administer independently if a valid physician order exists
options.B: A second nurse must independently verify patient identity, medication, dose, route, and time, with both nurses signing the controlled drug register
options.C: The ward pharmacist must be present at administration
options.D: Verbal confirmation from the charge nurse is sufficient

mcq_questions.explanation: UAE DHA and DOH medication safety standards require dual-nurse independent verification before administration of controlled Schedule I/II medications. Both nurses sign the controlled drug register (paper or electronic).

mcq_questions.question: A serious adverse event (sentinel event) occurs in a DHA-licensed hospital. What is the mandatory reporting timeframe?

options.B: Report at the next monthly quality meeting
options.C: Report to the NHRA Bahrain within 24 hours
options.D: Report to DHA via the Sheryan system within 24 hours

mcq_questions.explanation: DHA Patient Safety and Risk Management Policy mandates that serious adverse events (including sentinel events) be reported through the Sheryan e-portal within 24 hours. Failure to report is a professional and legal violation.

mcq_questions.question: A non-Arabic-speaking patient in a Dubai hospital does not understand the consent form presented in Arabic. What is the nurse's correct action?

options.A: Ask the patient's family member to translate the form and proceed
options.B: Document that the patient was educated and proceed with the procedure
options.C: Arrange for an official translation service to provide information in the patient's language before obtaining consent
options.D: Obtain a physician signature in lieu of patient consent

mcq_questions.explanation: UAE DHA/DOH Patient Rights policies guarantee patients the right to receive information in a language they understand. UAE is multilingual; official translation services must be provided — using untrained family members for clinical translation is not an acceptable substitute for complex consent discussions.

mcq_questions.question: Under UAE Federal Law No. 4 of 2016 on Medical Liability, what is a nurse's individual liability status?

options.A: Nurses have no individual liability — only the hospital bears responsibility
options.B: Nurses are individually liable for their clinical decisions within their scope of practice
options.C: Nurses are liable only if a physician countersigns the order
options.D: Liability applies only to DHA-licensed nurses, not DOH

mcq_questions.explanation: UAE Federal Law No. 4 of 2016 establishes individual liability for all healthcare professionals, including nurses, for negligent practice within their scope. The law applies across all UAE emirates.

mcq_questions.question: A standard Registered Nurse (RN) working under a DHA licence wishes to start prescribing paracetamol for a patient's pain. What is required?

options.A: A verbal instruction from the charge nurse is sufficient
options.B: The RN may prescribe common medications independently
options.C: A physician order is required; prescribing is not within standard RN scope — NP licensure is needed
options.D: The RN can prescribe after 5 years of clinical experience

mcq_questions.explanation: Prescribing authority is not within standard RN scope in the UAE under DHA or DOH. Only Nurse Practitioners (NPs) with specific NP licensure have prescribing authority. All other RNs require a physician order before administering any medication.

mcq_questions.question: A nurse notices that a documentation error was made in a patient's electronic medical record in a DHA facility. The correct approach is to:

options.A: Delete the incorrect entry and retype it correctly
options.B: Use the system's amendment/addendum function to correct the entry with date, time, and nurse's identifier
options.C: Ask the physician to make the correction on the nurse's behalf
options.D: Leave it unchanged to preserve the original record

mcq_questions.explanation: Under UAE Federal Law 4/2016, medical records are legal documents. Error corrections must be made transparently — in electronic records, this means using the system's amendment or addendum function that preserves the original entry and records who made the correction, when, and why. Deleting or overwriting is falsification.

mcq_questions.question: A patient in a DOH-licensed (Abu Dhabi) hospital refuses a recommended blood transfusion on religious grounds. The patient is alert, oriented, and legally competent. What is the nurse's correct action?

options.A: Override the refusal as it is a life-threatening decision
options.B: Contact the patient's family to persuade them to change the patient's mind
options.C: Respect the patient's right to refuse, document the refusal thoroughly, notify the physician, and escalate to the ethics committee if needed
options.D: Administer the transfusion while the patient is distracted

mcq_questions.explanation: A competent adult patient has the legal right to refuse treatment, including blood transfusions, under UAE patient rights frameworks. The nurse must document the refusal, notify the physician, and escalate as per facility policy (ethics committee). Overriding a competent refusal is a violation of patient autonomy and UAE law.

mcq_questions.question: Which of the following describes the DHA Senior Nurse classification compared to a General Nurse?

options.A: Senior Nurse may prescribe medications independently
options.B: Senior Nurse has a higher level of clinical experience but prescribing still requires NP licensure
options.C: Senior Nurse and General Nurse have identical scopes of practice
options.D: Senior Nurse classification is no longer used under current DHA policy

mcq_questions.explanation: DHA nursing scope of practice categories (General Nurse, Senior Nurse, Specialist Nurse, Nurse Practitioner) each have progressively expanded clinical roles, but prescribing authority is only granted at the Nurse Practitioner level. Senior Nurses have greater experience and supervisory responsibility but cannot prescribe.

mcq_questions.question: In a DHA-licensed facility, a nurse receives a verbal order by phone from a physician. What is the correct action?

options.A: Implement the order immediately without documentation until the physician arrives
options.B: Refuse all verbal orders as they are not permitted in UAE facilities
options.C: Document the verbal order immediately, read it back to the physician for confirmation, and ensure the physician countersigns it as soon as possible
options.D: Ask the charge nurse to verify and sign the verbal order

mcq_questions.explanation: While verbal and telephone orders are permitted in urgent situations in UAE facilities, the nurse must document the order immediately, perform a read-back to confirm accuracy, and ensure the physician countersigns the order promptly. This protects patient safety and complies with UAE medical liability standards.

mcq_questions.question: What patient identifiers are used before medication administration in DHA/DOH-licensed facilities?

options.B: Patient name and date of birth or medical record number

mcq_questions.explanation: UAE DHA and DOH medication safety standards require two patient identifiers before every medication administration: patient name and date of birth, or patient name and medical record number. Room or bed number is NOT an acceptable patient identifier.

mcq_questions.question: A MERS-CoV-positive patient is admitted to a DHA hospital. The nurse must perform suctioning (aerosol-generating procedure). Which personal protective equipment is required?

options.B: N95 respirator, eye protection, gown, and gloves
options.C: Surgical mask, eye shield, and apron only
options.D: No additional PPE beyond standard precautions

mcq_questions.explanation: MERS-CoV requires Standard + Droplet + Contact precautions. For aerosol-generating procedures such as suctioning, an N95 (or FFP2/3) respirator must replace the surgical mask. Eye protection (goggles or face shield), gown, and gloves complete the PPE set. A negative pressure room should be used if available.
